name: GCSE Physics equation sheet
summary: The equations a GCSE Physics or Combined Science candidate is given in the exam, 2025 to 2027.
subject: Physics
verified_note: The equations in the DfE GCSE physics content, which AQA, Edexcel and OCR each print on their own 2025 to 2027 sheet in their own order and words. H marks Higher tier; “Physics only” marks one not asked in Combined Science. Not yet compared line by line with each board’s PDF, so marked unverified.

lines.name: Work done
lines.math: work done = force × distance along the line of the force   W = Fs

lines.name: Moment
lines.math: moment = force × perpendicular distance from the pivot   M = Fd

lines.name: Uniform acceleration
lines.note: v the final velocity, u the initial velocity, s the distance

lines.name: Elastic potential energy
lines.note: while the limit of proportionality is not passed

lines.name: Specific heat capacity
lines.note: thermal energy change = mass × specific heat capacity × temperature change

lines.name: Specific latent heat
lines.note: energy for a change of state = mass × specific latent heat

lines.name: Efficiency
lines.math: efficiency = <sup>useful output energy transfer</sup>⁄<sub>total input energy transfer</sub> = <sup>useful power output</sup>⁄<sub>total power input</sub>

lines.name: Force on a wire
lines.note: force = magnetic flux density × current × length

lines.name: Transformer power
lines.note: a transformer that wastes no energy

name: GCSE Chemistry periodic table
summary: The periodic table a GCSE Chemistry or Combined Science candidate is given in the exam.
subject: Chemistry
verified_note: The facts of the periodic table insert AQA prints (docs/history/106): atomic number, symbol, name and relative atomic mass, the masses whole except chlorine and copper, and in brackets for an element with no stable isotope. Elements 58 to 71 and from 90 on are left out, as the insert leaves them out. Written from memory and not yet compared box by box with the insert, so marked unverified.

name: OCR GCSE Chemistry periodic table
summary: The periodic table on the Data Sheet an OCR GCSE Chemistry A (Gateway) candidate is given in the exam.
subject: Chemistry
verified_note: Copied box by box from the periodic table on OCR’s J248 Data Sheet (Autumn 2021), masses to one decimal place as it prints them, and none for an element with no stable isotope; its lanthanoid and actinoid rows are left out, as the GCSE table here leaves them (521). Checked against the Data Sheet text, not yet by a person, so marked unverified.

name: A level Chemistry periodic table
summary: The periodic table of the Data Booklet an AQA A level Chemistry candidate is given in the exam.
subject: Chemistry
verified_note: Copied box by box from the periodic table in AQA’s 7405 Data Booklet (the specimen insert; the booklet names itself the insert of every 7405 paper), masses to one decimal place and in brackets for an element with no stable isotope, the f-block underneath. The booklet’s spectroscopy tables are not here (521). Checked against the booklet text, not yet by a person, so marked unverified.
